errors.text: The critical transition is incorrectly placed at approximately 400–600 K; the target identifies 900 K as the threshold for rapid lattice disorder and sharply reduced wear resistance.

The proposed temperature-dependent reduction in stacking-fault energy, twinning suppression, and promotion of cross-slip/climb is not established by the cited evidence and is not the target mechanism.
The hypothesis reverses common stacking-fault-energy logic by associating high SFE with stabilized deformation twinning and reduced SFE with easier cross-slip.
The proposed experiment stops at 800 K and therefore cannot observe or falsify the target transition beginning at 900 K.
